content.title: UCLA beats Duke to return to Final Four: Live updates and reaction from Women’s March Madness 2026 Elite Eight game
content.text: The Bruins trailed by eight at halftime but dominated the second half to knock off the Blue DevilsLauren Betts and her UCLA teammates react after beating Duke. Getty ImagesUCLA headed back to Final Four Getty ImagesUCLA has been working all season to get back to the Final Four, and it earned another trip to today with its win over Duke. Our Grace Raynor on the Bruins' win over the Blue Devils.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementYour browser does not support the video tag.UCLA head coach Cori Close getting the final cut and chant to close the regional championship for UCLA. Devon Henderson / The AthleticKiki Rice and Gabriela Jacquez and their families with the Regional trophyUCLA's updated projectionsPer The Athletic’s updated bracket projections, UCLA has a 61 percent chance to advance to the national championship, regardless of its semifinal opponent.UCLA has a 19 percent probability of winning the title. Final stats Getty ImagesFG:Duke: 24-of-62UCLA: 29-of-583FG:Duke: 1-of-13UCLA: 2-of-14Rebounds:Duke: 26UCLA: 38Assists:Duke: 16UCLA: 16Turnovers:Duke: 13UCLA: 18Points in Paint: Duke: 32UCLA: 54Largest lead:Duke: 10UCLA: 12UCLA dancing to the Final Four Getty ImagesTo cap off their Final Four berth, the Golden 1 Center played the track Betts, Leger-Walker and Gabriela Jaquez learned a dance to last month so the trio could have an encore performance, just as it did at the Big Ten tournament.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCan UCLA get one step further?Last year, UCLA fell in the women’s Final Four to eventual champion UConn.Sarah Strong led UConn with 22 points, while Paige Bueckers added 16.UCLA will have a chance at avenging that defeat should the Bruins and Huskies win their respective Final Four semifinal games. Today’s results Getty Images Here are the Elite Eight results today in the women’s NCAA Tournament. Both of the No. 1 seeds survived and advanced to the Final Four.(1) UConn 70, (6) Notre Dame 52(1) UCLA 70, (3) Duke 58 Duke falling short again Getty ImagesFor the second consecutive season, Duke falls short in the Elite Eight. The Blue Devils put up a great fight today but just couldn’t overcome Lauren Betts.Duke’s women’s team hasn’t reached the Final Four since 1996. Lauren Betts' fatherYour browser does not support the video tag.Lauren Betts’ father has the nice custom jersey with both Lauren and Sienna’s numbers on it.What's next for UCLA? Getty ImagesUCLA will face either Texas or Michigan in the Final. Texas is the only team to defeat UCLA this season.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFinal scoring leaders Getty Images Below are the final scoring leaders for Duke and UCLA:Duke: Taina Mair (21 points, 8-of-16 FG, 1-of-5 3FG)UCLA: Lauren Betts (23 points, 9-of-14 FG)All-regional team Getty ImagesBelow is the all-regional team:MOP Lauren BettsAngela DugalićTaina MairToby Fournier MiLaysia FulwileyLauren Betts the differenceRecycling something I said after TCU won last night. In the end, while Duke fought hard going into halftime leading, one team had Lauren Betts (23 points, 10 rebounds), and the other team simply did not.Lauren Betts: 'I’m just so proud of everybody' Getty ImagesLauren Betts lets out a big scream after her postgame interview. You can tell that she and her teammates are hyped to be headed to Phoenix for the Final Four. 💬 “I’m just so proud of this team and their perseverance. Our mental toughness. “We were going to come up with some defensive stops. I’m just so proud of everybody.” FINAL: UCLA to the Final Four Getty ImagesQ4 0:00 - UCLA 70, Duke 58That will do it from Sacramento. UCLA is headed to the Final Four for the second consecutive season.It wasn’t easy against Duke after the Blue Devils led at halftime. But a dominant second-half from the Bruins has them advancing. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementKara Lawson is calling off the fight. 26 seconds left, and UCLA is going to wrap this one up.Final Four chants coming from UCLA fans behind us here.UCLA can taste victory Getty ImagesQ4 0:54.4 - UCLA 68, Duke 58Another layup for Lauren Betts and UCLA retains its 10-point advantage.The Bruins can taste victory with less than a minute to go.There was an exasperated look on Duke coach Kara Lawson's face, if only for a second, after that Taina Mair airball down seven with a minute remaining. Looked as if she was accepting defeat for about all of about one second before she turned back around and began yelling at her guards to come up and press in the frontcourt.
